Incident Bot: :wave: PAGE: Elevated token latency and queueing observed in hosted-eu (INC-20260314-11). 95th > 1s, p99 ~1.8s, error-rate nominal. Dashboard: https://dash.team/redwood/INC-20260314-11
Jules K.: saw the page while wrapping handoff. I can stay on for 30m as secondary. Samir, can you pick up primary?
Samir P.: taking primary for 90m. Logging in. Any immediate customer impact?
Nina H.: we have a spike in small-chat payloads to /generate-stream that increased concurrent streams by 3x starting 09:11 UTC. Token throughput per-request down but total tokens up. Might be batching inefficiency.
Ravi M.: looking at runtime traces — batching window shrunk to 25ms under load, causing many tiny batches. Also noticed a recent deploy to the batching service an hour ago (rev: batch-service@20260314.1).
Samir P.: runbook: eng-oncall/runbooks/batching-tuning.md -> steps: 1) temporarily increase batching window 2) enable continuous batching flag for generation 3) if no improvement, route lower-tier traffic to quantized model.
Jules K.: I can patch the config to increase batch_window_ms: from 25 -> 100. Applying now: `kubectl -n inference patch cm batch-config -p '{"data":{"batch_window_ms":"100"}}'`
Jules K.: patch applied, rolling restart of batch-worker set.
Runbook Bot: Runbook step executed: increased batch window. Monitor p95/p99 and average batch size for 10m.
Nina H.: avg batch size jumped from 1.8 -> 6.4 within 2 minutes. p95 dropped ~30%. Good signal.
Samir P.: I'm toggling continuous batching on for generation nodes: `env CONTINUOUS_BATCHING=true` pushed.
Ravi M.: also enabling degraded routing to variant-lite for non-enterprise plans, to reduce pressure on full model replicas. Command: `POST /routing/set {scope: "non-enterprise", target: "variant-lite"}`
Samir P.: applied degraded routing for non-enterprise scope. Notifying support to suppress alerts for affected customers.
Coverage Bot: Noted: primary oncall for APAC coverage missing between 02:00-05:00 UTC nights. Created ticket: COVER-1091.
Jules K.: Filing incident follow-ups: TICKET-4301 "Investigate batching-service deploy impact" assigned to eng-runtime; TICKET-4302 "Tune default batching window based on request distribution" assigned to eng-platform; TICKET-4303 "Customer communications: brief note to affected tenants" assigned to support.
Nina H.: FYI — saw one anomalous client spamming small requests from ip 18.203.45.7 -> flagged in TICKET-4304 for product/security to review.
Samir P.: status after 12m: p95 improved to 420ms, p99 ~720ms, average batch size stable ~5. I'll remain primary until Jules signs off or until 10:45 UTC.
Jules K.: good progress. I'm going to hand primary to Samir for the next 90m (confirmed). My action items before I leave: 1) update incident log with timeline and commands executed 2) attach Grafana snapshots 3) create follow-up retro invite.
Incident Bot: Retro meeting scheduled: 2026-03-16 16:00 UTC. Invitees: Samir P., Jules K., Nina H., Ravi M., eng-runtime.
Samir P.: leaving checklist: ensure tickets created (listed above), alert thresholds adjusted to avoid noise, and add a runbook note to verify batch-service deploy gating. I'll add that to TICKET-4301.
Jules K.: marking mitigations as effective. Condition to close: p99 < 800ms for 20 minutes and no tail-of-queue backlog.
Nina H.: 20m check-in: p99 610ms, queue length normalized. Logging final metrics.
Samir P.: closing thread now and adding summary to INC-20260314-11 page. Leaving as primary -> handing to oncall rotation. Last_message_ts: 2130000123.
